title.narrative: Sri Lanka - Improving Monitoring and Evaluation of Samurdhi Safety Net Program

description.narrative: The objective of the IDF grant is to support the institutional development of the Division of Samurdhi through the adoption of an ICT-based Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) System. Such a system will include the development of a beneficiary database and computerized reporting and record-keeping systems at all levels of program operation. The Management Information System (MIS) is expected to facilitate budgeting and planning with regards to resource allocation for the cash transfer components of the program. The IDF grant will be used to design and pilot the new MIS in three selected locations. It is expected that the experiences of these locations will then form the basis for the scaling up of the MIS across all the Divisions where the cash transfer program operates. In addition, the IDF would build Samurdhi' institutional capacity to evaluate the effectiveness of the Samurdhi program, particularly its targeting. The objective of the Institutional Development Fund (IDF) grant is to finance the development and adoption of a comprehensive Management Information System (MIS) for the Samurdhi food stamp and cash transfer program (FSCTP), Sri Lanka's largest transfer program. The proposed MIS, underpinned by a systems assessment, will be implemented via the development of necessary software and building staff capacity with the goal of improving the overall institutional capacity of the Samurdhi Commissioner General's Department (SCGD) to monitor and evaluate the program. The proposed MIS will include the development of an eligible households and beneficiary database, and computerized reporting, financial monitoring and record-keeping systems at all levels of program operation. The MIS is expected to improve the administrative efficiency and to help facilitate a more poverty-based budgeting and planning of the FSCTP component of the Samurdhi program. The proposed IDF grant will be used to design and pilot the new MIS in three selected locations. The Government of Sri Lanka (GoSL) has committed funds to replicate the system in three additional locations. It is expected that the experiences of these six locations, upon evaluation, will help form the basis for the scaling up of the MIS across all other locations across the country where the program operates.
